faithfulness_note: Read all 24 sampled reviews (full census, n_total=24): roughly 5-6 are clear Coinbase chart-disappeared/froze/wrong-data-after-update complaints, matching the stated 'roughly 6-7 of 24, mostly Coinbase' and the honest 'no single theme is a majority' hedge; the rest is genuinely a mix of dividend-calendar/benchmark/candlestick feature requests and general praise as described. clarity_note: Title names the dominant-but-minority bug theme and the description explicitly clarifies it is not a majority, so a PM would not mistake this for a single unified complaint.
usefulness_note: Flags a real 'chart broke after update' regression pattern (actionable bug) alongside a useful catalog of recurring charting feature asks (dividend calendar requested 4x, candlesticks, benchmark comparison).

faithfulness_note: Independent keyword-based re-scan of chart+failure language found ~27-30/150 chart loading/freezing/lagging complaints (vs. claimed 39/150), with Coinbase at ~60-63% share (vs. claimed 59%) - directionally correct and in a plausible range once phrasings my regex missed (e.g. 'charts NEVER work') are added back in; not an overstated majority since the write-up correctly says it's the largest theme, not a majority. All 3 quotes verified verbatim in their source reviews.
clarity_note: Title and description clearly scope this to load/freeze/stale-data bugs specifically, distinct from feature requests, and correctly caveat it's a plurality not a majority.
usefulness_note: A concentrated, technically specific bug pattern (chart rendering pipeline, heavily Coinbase) is exactly the kind of signal an eng team could triage directly.

faithfulness_note: Manually classified the first 50/150 sampled reviews by hand (not just keyword matching) and found ~26/50 (52%) genuinely describe frozen/held/restricted funds blocking transfer, sale, withdrawal or unstaking - an exact match to the claimed 52% (78/150). Both spot-checked quotes (unstaking delay, 6-day hold) verified verbatim and consistent with their full review context.
clarity_note: Title and description precisely name the mechanism (locked/frozen/delayed access), the affected actions (transfer/withdraw/sell/unstake), the timeframe (days to weeks), and the platform concentration (Coinbase) - unambiguous to a PM.
usefulness_note: This is a severe, recurring trust/ops issue (funds inaccessible for days-weeks plus unresponsive support) that is unambiguously actionable and non-redundant with other clusters in this batch.

faithfulness_note: Read ~110/150 sampled reviews. The 62% positive-sentiment figure is plausible, but the description frames essentially all of that majority as praise 'for being an easy, beginner-friendly way to get started' - in the actual sample, well under half of the positive reviews explicitly invoke beginner/new/starting language (e.g. 'Best crypto app!', 'Fantastic platform for crypto', 'it's the app for crypto'); the rest is generic crypto-app positivity with no beginner framing at all. The title/description conflate generic praise with beginner-specific praise, overstating how much of the cluster is really about onboarding ease. Quotes themselves (verified verbatim) were cherry-picked from the genuinely beginner-flavored subset, which is not representative of the bucket as a whole.
clarity_note: The title promises a specific 'beginner entry point' narrative, but a PM reading only title+description would not realize that much of the underlying '62%' is undifferentiated generic praise rather than beginner-specific commentary.
usefulness_note: Largely restates positive sentiment already covered by ONBOARDING_BEGINNER clusters 0/2/4 in this same batch; as a standalone roadmap item it adds little new action beyond 'keep crypto onboarding simple.'

faithfulness_note: First 60/150 reviews manually reviewed: the large majority genuinely praise ease/speed/reliability of buying, selling, and trading crypto as described, and coin-variety requests appear at roughly the stated minority rate (~5 in the first 60, close to the claimed ~6/150 overall).
clarity_note: Title and description clearly state this is general satisfaction with core buy/sell/trade mechanics plus a small variety-of-coins ask, with no overreach.
usefulness_note: Mostly a 'things are fine' signal with limited direct action beyond the minor coin-variety request; useful as context but not a strong standalone roadmap driver.

usefulness_note: Useful confirmation that Learn-and-Earn is a loyalty driver worth protecting/expanding, with an early warning that reduced reward frequency causes friction.

faithfulness_note: Manual read of first 40 of 140 reviews (full sample, n_total=140) overwhelmingly matches the 'Learn and Earn as onboarding driver' description, including the negative quote which is genuinely negative overall ('I would give it 0 stars') and matches the description's caveat about incorrect/missing payouts. faithfulness_note: App split (Coinbase 65 / Robinhood 68 / Trading 212 17) verified exactly. However, the specific claim that 'about half of the sample (72/150) uses the explicit word beginner/novice/newbie' does not hold up: a direct keyword count against the prep file (case-insensitive, including plural/typo forms like 'beginn*', 'novice', 'newb*') finds only 61-62/150 (41%), not 72/150 (48%) - a measurable overstatement of a precisely-stated number, even though the broader qualitative claim (terse cross-platform beginner praise) is accurate.
clarity_note: Title and description are otherwise clear and well-scoped (terse positive statements, roughly even app split, small pushback minority), undermined only by the inaccurate specific statistic.
usefulness_note: Confirms an already-established pattern (beginner-friendliness) at a coarse, terse-review level; the minority 'not enough help' complaints (a real, findable subset in the data) are the most actionable part but are given only a passing one-clause mention.
